checks.diagnosis: The prompt permits cuts that split a verb (or verbal phrase) from the words that complete its object or complement, producing misleading or contradiction-prone preceding fragments.
checks.evidence: en_us_381, en_us_633, en_us_936, en_us_738 — each policy kept a cut immediately after a verb or verbal phrase while the following words complete its object/complement; the offline target keeps the verb+object together.
checks.type_predicate: Positions immediately after a verb or verbal phrase where the next words continue or complete that verb's direct object or complement (the object/complement begins at the next word).

edit.text: Do not cut between a verb (or verbal phrase) and its object/complement; keep the verb plus its object/complement in the same segment.

orders.diagnosis: When two candidate cuts lie in the same clause, the prompt sometimes prefers an earlier intra-clause cut over the later cut that completes the clause's predicate, worsening cohesion.
orders.evidence: en_us_633, en_us_381, en_us_1116 — in each sentence the prompt preferred an earlier cut that splits predicate structure while the offline target prefers the later cut that yields a self-contained preceding predicate.
orders.type_predicate: Sentences where two candidate cuts occur inside the same clause and one cut falls between a verb and its object/complement while the other falls after the object/complement (both markers present).

edit.text: When two cuts are inside the same clause and one completes the clause's predicate while the other splits the predicate and its object, prefer the later, predicate-completing cut.
